title: Dynamical Tensor Train Approximation for Wigner--Fokker--Planck Equation with Applications to Open Quantum Systems
abstract: We develop a dynamical tensor-train method for the Wigner--Fokker--Planck equation arising in continuous-variable open quantum systems. The Wigner function is evolved directly in tensor-train form using a projector-splitting integrator, while the nonlocal Wigner pseudo-differential operator is treated through low-rank representations of the potential difference and matrix-free exponential actions. The resulting method avoids full tensor-product computations in high-dimensional phase space. Numerical experiments in one, two, and three spatial dimensions demonstrate the accuracy and scalability of the method, including simulations in a six-dimensional phase space.
summary: This paper introduces a novel dynamical tensor-train approximation to solve the Wigner–Fokker–Planck equation for open quantum systems. By representing the high-dimensional Wigner function using low-rank tensor formats, the method bypasses the exponential scaling associated with full phase-space discretization. This allows for accurate and scalable simulations in complex, high-dimensional quantum regimes.
main_problem: Developing an efficient numerical method to simulate the Wigner–Fokker–Planck (WFP) equation for open quantum systems in high-dimensional phase space.
main_result: The proposed dynamical tensor-train method successfully simulates the WFP equation in high dimensions (up to six dimensions) by avoiding full tensor-product computations.
method: The method employs a projector-splitting integrator applied to the Wigner function represented in a Tensor-Train (TT) format, treating the nonlocal pseudo-differential operator via low-rank approximations.
model_or_system: The system is an open quantum system whose evolution is governed by the Wigner–Fokker–Planck (WFP) equation, which includes terms for free transport, potential interaction ($\Theta[V]$), and various diffusion/friction terms.
key_observables: The Wigner function $W(t, x, p)$ in phase space.
important_parameters: Diffusion coefficients ($D_{pp}, D_{xx}, D_{xp}$), friction coefficient ($\gamma$), and the effective TT rank ($r$).
main_assumptions: The Wigner function and potential difference are assumed to admit low-rank tensor representations (TT/CP), and the method uses a first-order projector-splitting time discretization.
paper_structure: The paper first defines the WFP equation and its components, identifies the curse of dimensionality, and then details the tensor-train decomposition and the projector-splitting time integration scheme to handle the evolution step-by-step.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the computational bottleneck of simulating open quantum dynamics in high dimensions, which is a major challenge in quantum optics and open quantum systems research.
